metrics.name: Realized hours per phone per working day
metrics.def: Accepted hours are the hours we are paid for. This number is the accepted hours that one deployed phone made on a day when its site ran a shift.
metrics.how: Take the accepted hours for the day. Divide them by the number of phones deployed at sites that ran a shift that day. Recorded hours do not count until review has checked them and kept them.
metrics.owner: Mano, in the evening number. The hours come from the wrap reports. The review decisions come from Youssef Medhat.
metrics.read: The shift length is the highest this number can be. The lowest it should be is the month's target divided by the deployed phones and the working days. If the number is under that, first check active phones against deployed phones. Then check flags. A gap between active and deployed means some phones were not used. Flags mean footage was deleted.

metrics.name: Backlog in device-days
metrics.def: Footage that a phone recorded but has not uploaded yet. We count it in device-days. One device-day is one phone holding a full day of footage.
metrics.how: For each phone at the site, look at how much footage it still holds. Write it as a share of one day's shift. Add up the shares. Two phones that each hold half a day make one device-day.
metrics.owner: The Portfolio Manager, for each site, in the wrap report. Each night, the hub attendants write down the devices that are still at the hub.
metrics.read: After the flush, the number should be zero. If any site is over one, that is an incident. Moharam hears about it the same night. No device keeps more than one day of footage overnight.

metrics.name: Flags per 1,000 hours
metrics.def: The number of review notes for every 1,000 hours uploaded. A flag is one note on one video. A flag is either feedback or fraud.
metrics.how: Take the flags in the week. Divide them by the hours uploaded in the week. Multiply by 1,000. Show feedback flags on one line and fraud flags on another line. Then show both together.
metrics.owner: Youssef Medhat, every week, for each site and for each worker.
metrics.read: The number should go down every week. If it goes up at one site, the problem is at that site. If it goes up at every site, the problem is in the briefing. A worker's own flag count matters more than any rate. A second strike pauses the device. Three flags remove the worker. A fraud flag means nobody is paid for that footage.

metrics.name: Catch-before-client rate
metrics.def: Take every video that gets a flag in the end. This number is the share of those videos that our own review caught before the client saw them.
metrics.how: Count the videos we flagged or deleted. Count the videos the client flagged after we passed them. Divide the first count by the two counts added together.
metrics.owner: Youssef Medhat, every month, before the invoice. The client's flags come through Adham. Nobody else talks to the client.
metrics.read: The good result is that we catch all of them. Then the client finds nothing that we missed. Every flag from the client is a miss. When we catch a video, we lose that video. When we miss a video, we lose that video and we put our work with the client in danger.

metrics.name: Active phones versus deployed phones
metrics.def: A deployed phone is a phone on the registry at a site. An active phone is a phone that uploaded today. The difference is the phones that were not used.
metrics.how: Count the phones at the site that uploaded today. Divide by the phones on the registry at that site today. Spare phones in the pool do not count as deployed. Partner phones are counted the same way.
metrics.owner: The Portfolio Manager, for each site, in the wrap report. The quartermaster keeps the deployed count correct.
metrics.read: The good result is that every deployed phone is active. If a phone is dark by noon, its operator goes to the phone. The Portfolio Manager hears about it in the same hour. If the fleet is short at 6 PM, there is a call the same night. It does not wait until the next morning.

metrics.name: Hours by environment category
metrics.def: Accepted hours, split by the kind of place where they were filmed. The kinds are factory, hotel, warehouse, construction site, and farm.
metrics.how: Every site gets one environment tag from sourcing. Add that site's accepted hours to the line for its tag.
metrics.owner: Mano, every week, in the numbers that go into the client update and the sourcing target list.
metrics.read: There is no good total for this number. There is only a good mix. We choose sites for the categories they add, not only for the hours. When a line stops growing, the next site goes into that category.
